name: The Ozolith
oracle_text:
Whenever a creature you control leaves the battlefield, if it had counters on it, put those counters on The Ozolith.
At the beginning of combat on your turn, if The Ozolith has counters on it, you may move all counters from The Ozolith onto target creature.
blocked_sentences: Whenever a creature you control leaves the battlefield, if it had counters on it, put those counters on The Ozolith.
At the beginning of combat on your turn, if The Ozolith has counters on it, you may move all counters from The Ozolith onto target creature.

needs.what: A counter move that transfers EVERY kind of counter an object has at once, each kind keeping its own amount, rather than one named counter kind: 'put those counters on The Ozolith' and 'move all counters from The Ozolith onto target creature' both mean the whole multiset (+1/+1, -1/-1, loyalty-style, charge, oil, shield, indestructible, whatever the creature happened to carry). Concretely: an `all_kinds: true` (or omitted-`counter`) mode on `move_counters` that enumerates the source's counter kinds at resolution and moves each in full.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `move_counters` and `add_counters` are the closest ops, but every documented use names a single counter kind and a single amount (the packet's own worked example of a counter read, `counters_on`, is likewise keyed by `{"counter": "charge"}`). Authoring The Ozolith against a one-kind move would force picking `+1/+1` and silently dropping every other counter type the card is printed to carry - exactly the quiet near-miss the brief forbids. `proliferate` adds to counters that already exist and cannot relocate any.

needs.what: A way to use the counters an object had as it left the battlefield as the SOURCE of a counter move. The `leaves_battlefield` trigger's creature is already gone when the ability resolves, so the effect needs its last-known counter multiset as a movable quantity - e.g. `move_counters` accepting `{"from": {"trigger_source": true}}` resolved against last-known information, or a `snapshot` that captures a whole counter set (not one scalar) for a later `add_counters`/`move_counters` to spend.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `counters_had` exists in `value_keys` and covers the intervening-if ('if it had counters on it' as a `cmp` of `counters_had` against `{"const": 0}`), but it is a value read that yields one number for one counter kind - it cannot name the set of kinds, so it cannot drive the transfer. `snapshot` is documented as how a card reads *a value* after its target has left, and the packet's notes state flatly that 'there is no general last-known-information system', so no existing op can point a counter move at a departed permanent.
